whatItDoes: Estimates the monthly payment, total interest, and full payoff term for a fixed-rate mortgage. Uses standard amortization math to model what a home loan really costs, including how extra payments can shorten the term and cut total interest.
whyItExists: A mortgage is the largest debt most households take on, and the gap between interest rates and terms can shift the total cost by hundreds of thousands. An amortization calculator makes the real price of a loan visible before you commit.
whoShouldUse: Homebuyers, real-estate agents, financial planners, and anyone comparing mortgage offers or payoff paths before signing.
useCases: Estimate a mortgage monthly payment for a target home price
Compare the total interest of a shorter vs. longer term
Model additional payments that shorten the payoff term and save interest
Check how a rate change shifts the total mortgage cost
Decide between a 15-year and 30-year mortgage for your budget
See how much interest a biweekly payment schedule could save
instructions: Enter the home price you plan to finance
Enter the annual mortgage interest rate as a percent
Choose the term in years (15 and 30 are common)
Read the monthly payment, total interest, and payoff term
Add a monthly extra payment to see how much sooner the loan pays off
Compare term lengths side by side before choosing
examples: $350,000 at 6.5% for 30 years → payment ≈ $2,212, total interest ≈ $446,000
$350,000 at 6.5% for 15 years → payment ≈ $3,050, total interest ≈ $199,000
$750,000 at 5.75% for 30 years → payment ≈ $4,376, total interest ≈ $825,000
$350,000 at 6.5% for 30 years with an extra $200/month → payoff cut by several years and interest saved by tens of thousands
bestPractices: Compare the total-interest rows, not only the payment
Only choose the shorter term if the higher payment is definitely affordable
Add property tax, insurance, and HOA fees on top of the payment for the true monthly cost
Re-run the numbers if rates move by a quarter point
Treat extra payments as a way to shorten the term while keeping the option to pause them
commonMistakes: Leaving out property tax, insurance, and HOA in the budget
Financing up to the top of an approval range without a rate buffer
Basing a decision on a teaser rate that expires before closing
Assuming an adjustable term behaves like a fixed 30-year loan
Ignoring how private mortgage insurance (PMI) adds cost when the down payment is under 20%
faq: Does this tool support multiple currencies? — Yes, select your currency from the dropdown. All calculations run locally in your browser.
Does this include escrow for taxes and insurance? — No, it covers principal and interest only.
What does total interest mean? — The portion of all your payments that goes to the lender as interest.
Can I model a shorter term? — Yes, set the term to 15 or 20 years to compare payoffs.
Is my data shared? — No, every calculation runs locally in your browser.
How do extra payments help? — They go straight to principal, so less interest accrues and the loan is paid off sooner.
Should I refinance if rates drop? — Compare your current remaining term against a new loan's total interest and closing costs before deciding.
features: Monthly payment, total interest, and payoff term
Adjustable home price, rate, and term
assumptions: Fixed-rate mortgage amortization; property tax/insurance excluded. US-centric defaults (30-year term) but math is generic.
